items: Transcripts: “Choose what goes in the file” can now save a Word document (.docx) or a PDF, with the same choices: style, speakers’ names, time stamps, clean or every word, tags. Both are made on this computer.

Transcripts: saved files now follow more of the chosen style. Rev legal writes “Exhibit 5” and “Page 15” in digits, numbers from 11 in digits, “$42” for “forty two dollars”, years in digits, “going to” for “gonna”, and a spaced double dash for a cut-off word. The transcript itself keeps what was heard.

Transcripts: tags. A row above the transcript offers the style’s own tags: [inaudible] (with the time, for Rev legal), a guess, [crosstalk], [laughter], foreign speech and more. Select the words, or leave it on the word being played, and press one. The heard words stay underneath; pressing the tag again takes it off.
Transcripts: saved files carry the tags in the chosen style’s wording, and “Choose what goes in the file” can also mark unsure words as guesses and silences of ten seconds or more.

Transcripts: “Choose what goes in the file”, at the top of Save as a file. Pick a style, and whether the file has the speakers’ names, a time stamp on each paragraph, and every word or the clean version, and see how it begins before you save. The transcript itself is never changed.

Transcripts: the Clean script now follows the matter’s style. Rev legal hides only “um”, “uh” and cut-off part-words; TranscribeMe clean hides fillers and a word said twice; TranscribeMe full hides nothing. Hidden words stay in the transcript.

Transcripts: Personal transcripts can now get punctuation and capitals, added by a small language model in the Reverb helper on this computer. Tick “Add punctuation and capitals afterwards” under Personal, or press “Add them on this computer” above a transcript that has none. No word is changed; it takes about as long as the recording.

Transcripts: matters. Give a recording a matter (a case or a job) and its other recordings share its cast from Legal, and, if you tick “Remember named voices”, a speaker you named once is recognised by voice and named in the rest. Voiceprints stay in this browser and “Forget voices” removes them.
Transcripts: a style per matter. With “Rev, legal”, automatic notations use Rev’s wording and digits (for example “(Exhibit 25 was marked for identification.)”).

Transcripts: “Set from the words”. When a transcript is finished, Mixtape names numbered speakers from what they say (who asks, who answers, who says the court’s words) and, in a legal transcript, puts in notations where an exhibit, an oath or a recess is heard. Everything it sets is highlighted and listed above the text with Keep and Undo. No AI, nothing leaves the computer.
Transcripts: Personal (Reverb) transcripts now have speakers. After Reverb writes the words down, Mixtape finds who speaks when on this computer; click a name to rename it everywhere.

Transcripts: when a recording follows a website, you can tick “Write down the whole recording now”. Only the part is shown and played; for the next part press “Part…” and choose it, with no new transcribing.
Transcripts: “My recording starts in the middle of the website’s”. Say where on the website your recording begins; the clock, the following and Backup Track all use it.
Transcripts now says so when Backup Track cannot be reached from the window Mixtape is open in, and what to do about it.

One audio, wherever you put it. If Backup Track has no audio of its own, tick Follow Backup Track and the recording here plays with its sound, following the website. If Backup Track has the audio, it makes the sound and the recording here follows silently. Never two sounds at once.

Transcripts: a recording that is already transcribed in full can be worked on in parts. Press Part in the player bar, find where the website's clip starts, and press Show only this part. Only that stretch is shown and played, counted from 0:00 like the website. Nothing is deleted: choose another part, or Show the whole recording, whenever you like.

Transcripts and Backup Track now stay the same in both directions: the start, the clock choice and the left-out stretches you set in the 'follow a website' form are set in Backup Track too (when it has the same recording).
The length on the website comes from Backup Track by itself, also in a Mixtape window that was already open when the extension was loaded or updated.
The two clock buttons always show which one is chosen.
Updates fetch every file fresh, so a new version can no longer keep an old stylesheet.

Transcripts: the 'follow a website' form now goes in the same steps as Backup Track. 1: play to the first words and press This part starts here. 2: choose whether the clock counts from 0:00 like the website. 3: the length on the website (shown by itself when Backup Track is following the site). A line then says the part is ready, and you press Transcribe.

Transcripts: point at a recording in the list and press the small ✕ to remove it from Mixtape, together with its transcript. It asks first and shows the recording's length. The original file on your computer is not touched.

Transcripts: when a transcript is to follow a website, you can list stretches the website leaves out that your recording still has. They are not written down, the clock does not count them, and playback jumps over them.
With Backup Track following the website, choosing Yes fills in the start, the website's length and the left-out stretches by itself. Nothing to type.

Transcripts now asks, before transcribing: is this to follow along with a website? If yes, find where the part starts by playing your recording (Play, back and forward buttons) and press This part starts here, or type the time. Say where it ends, or how long the website's part is.
With Backup Track installed, Take both from Backup Track fills in the start and the website's length for you.
Only that part is written down, and it counts from 0:00 like the website.
Transcripts can write down only a part of a recording. Before you press Transcribe, choose Only a part and say where it starts and ends (hours:minutes:seconds, or where the player is).
For a transcript of a part, Part's time in the player bar makes the clock, the slider and the times beside the paragraphs count from the start of the part, like a site that only has that part.
Personal (Reverb): choose your reverb-personal folder itself; and the helper can now start with Windows, so choosing Personal is all you do.

Transcripts has a cleaner layout, By speaker: each speaker's turn is its own block, with a coloured dot and the name on top and the words in a quiet box. Untick By speaker above the text to go back to one flowing page. Read-alongs are unchanged.

Transcripts can follow Backup Track (the browser extension). Tick Follow Backup Track in the player bar and the recording here, its picture and its lit word move with the site you are transcribing on, so you can see who is speaking. The switch only appears when the extension is installed.
Reader: OCR… reads scanned pages and pictures so you can search and copy their text. It makes a new PDF and tells you, page by page, how sure it was. It is machine reading: check names and numbers.

Reader: Redact now works correctly on pages that are stored sideways or upside down. Before this version, a blacked-out word on such a page could stay readable. If you redacted a turned page earlier, check that copy again.
Reader: Pages, Redact and OCR are together under Tools.
Transcripts has a Legal mode (the § Legal button). Type a short code such as ;ina and it becomes the standard wording with the time, or pick from Insert.
Exhibits propose the next number and build an exhibit index and a witness index by themselves.
Alt + 1 to 9 set the speaker; examination headings set up Q and A.
Presets for US company style, US court, US deposition, South Africa and the UK. Nothing is ever inserted or guessed for you.
When you forget songs in Privacy and storage, a Player that is open elsewhere drops them at once instead of still showing them.
Easier to use with the keyboard: menus and dialogs take the keyboard and give it back, every control shows where you are, and in the Cutter F6 moves between controls (Tab still plays and pauses).
Easier to read: faint text is darker, and boxes have clearer edges.
Works better on a phone: nothing runs off the side, and buttons are finger-sized.
Studio: the top bar wraps to a second line on smaller screens instead of pushing Export off the edge, and the tempo label no longer blocks clicks.

Transcripts asks what a transcript is for. Paid or client work uses Mixtape's own recogniser. Personal can use Rev's Reverb through a helper on your computer; Rev's licence allows that for personal use only, and the transcript says so.
The Reader now opens Word, Markdown, plain text, RTF, OpenDocument, ebooks (.epub) and screenplays (.fountain) in a comfortable reading view.
Pages…: turn, delete, reorder, merge, extract and split the pages of a PDF, with Undo.
Redact…: black out words or areas in a PDF. The words are removed, not covered, and the new file is checked before you can save it.
Every tool now has a way back to Mixtape's home page, where Privacy and storage also lives.
When Mixtape has been updated while you have it open, a small notice tells you and lets you reload when it suits you. It never reloads by itself.
Press ? in any tool to see its keys. The Player and the Reader now have a keys list too.
The first time you open a tool, a short welcome points at where to start. You can skip it, and bring it back from the keys list.
If something goes wrong, Mixtape says so in plain words and tells you what to do next. The technical detail stays on your device.
A home page shows all five tools and what each is for.
Privacy and storage shows everything Mixtape keeps on this device, backs it all up to one file, restores it, and can forget it.
Mixtape no longer connects to any other website. Its fonts and the speech recogniser are now part of the app itself.
Studio: a round of fixes so that nothing is lost when storage is blocked or a save fails.
Cutter: “Forget everything on this device” (under Keys and tips) removes everything the Cutter keeps in this browser. Files you saved and your library are not touched.
Cutter: a round of fixes.
Player: if a favourite, a playlist or a song could not be saved or removed, the Player now tells you instead of carrying on as if it had worked.
Transcripts: a file saved from a recording you marked sensitive says so in its name and at its top.
Transcripts: a correction you were half-way through typing is never dropped.
Transcripts: after a pause, Play picks up 10 seconds earlier so you can find your place. Back jumps 10 seconds, forward 5.
Fixes across all the tools so that nothing is lost, and nothing is sent anywhere, by accident.
Reader: every change is saved into the file as you make it. Undo takes a change back, and “Back to original” restores the file as you opened it.
Cutter: when you join files, you choose whether to save the list of where each clip begins.
Cutter: a joined file comes with a list of where each clip begins and ends.
Cutter: joining a hundred files at once now works.
New tool: the Reader. Open PDFs, highlight and add notes, fill in forms and sign, all offline.
Cutter: the back and forward keys jump 3 seconds unless you choose another step.
Cutter: Tab plays and pauses and Shift + Tab goes back, as in Transcripts. The arrow keys move back and forward, and change the volume.
An installed Mixtape still opens its saved pages when the website answers with an error.
